newsitem.title: UK: BA gains as Q3 profits top forecasts.
newsitem.headline: BA gains as Q3 profits top forecasts.

text.p: Shares in British Airways Plc rose in pre-market trading on Monday after the company posted better-than-expected third quarter results.
The stock was up 10-1/2p at 597 by 0824 GMT.
BA said its pre-tax profit rose 8.7 percent to 113 million stg in the third quarter from 104 million stg a year before on turnover which grew 6.4 percent to 2.016 billion stg from 1.895 billion.
Analysts had expected quarterly profits of around 100 million stg.

In a statement, chairman Sir Colin Marshall said the airline's one billion stg efficiency programme was on track and that he expected the economic trends which had boosted airline profits in 1996 to continue in through 1997.
James Halstead, analyst at Credit Lyonnais Laing, said the results were good, with weaker-than-expected revenues and passenger yields more than offset by greater-than-expected cost savings.
"The cost items were much better than expected," Halstead said, "with airlines a small change on the top line can mean a huge change on the bottom line."
At Paribas analyst Chris Avery welcomed the cost reductions BA had achieved against a background of rising fuel costs.

"These are very very good results," Avery said, though he said there would likely be costs associated with recently announced jobs cuts which made him reluctant to change his full-year profit forecast.
